content:
After consecutive days of land resumption operations, only a very small number of villagers remain in Cha Kwo Ling Village, yet some shop operators continue to run their businesses as usual, quietly awaiting the day when the land is handed over. Some neighbours said the Siu family had indeed lived in the village for several decades and described the arrested person as "born and raised there," though they recalled that after his mother moved away a few years ago, she still returned to the village from time to time.

After being arrested yesterday, he was granted bail. Police replied that Mr Siu was arrested on suspicion of "obstructing a public officer in the execution of his duties" and "criminal intimidation." The Lands Department said the villager had moved in after the population freeze registration was conducted, and had previously held public housing, thus not meeting the rehousing eligibility criteria.

Mrs Siu said today that her father-in-law passed away in 2019, and her husband and other siblings jointly inherited the land title through estate administration. About two years ago, the family signed off with the Lands Department on the land compensation, and it had been confirmed that no compensation would be given for the structures built on the land, yet to date they had not received a single cent. She revealed that her husband's sister, as one of the heirs, was also caught off guard by yesterday's events, as she had cooperated with the demolition and had earlier moved to transitional housing, and was likewise waiting for the compensation before she could decide on her next steps.

Not "refusing to leave and digging in"

Mrs Siu went on to say that the family had long planned to surrender the land and move away, and had intended to negotiate a moving date with the Lands Department; they were not "refusing to leave and digging in." She said that two weeks ago, the Civil Engineering and Development Department had also come to count the trees in the garden, describing that "everything has been proceeding in line with the normal process."

It was only when the "sudden land resumption" took place yesterday that her husband was accused of intimidating staff. Mrs Siu said she could not understand: "The Lands Department staff could actually have checked with my husband or my sister-in-law, as they are also among the heirs of this piece of land. Whether the compensation money has been paid, they could have verified it. Why didn't they check?" She criticised the department for overreach in law enforcement, and accused it of "inverting the facts."

According to a review of the information, regarding the current land policy compensation, for special ex-gratia compensation for old lots in New Kowloon and Hong Kong Island, the amount is calculated according to the special ex-gratia compensation rate based on the value of lots in the vicinity of the resumed land. Agricultural land owners may receive special ex-gratia compensation according to the first-tier agricultural land zonal compensation rate under the New Territories Land Ex-gratia Zonal Compensation System (HK$1,043 per square foot).

Reporters asked some social work teams of the new development areas in office at the time, and regarding the current land policy compensation, even if the affected households affected by land resumption themselves own property, this does not conflict with the land compensation. If they are public housing tenants, an asset review will be conducted after the land is sold to determine whether they fall foul of the "well-off public housing tenants" policy.

Lands Department once said it would provide buffer time as far as practicable

The Lands Department said in its reply yesterday that on 12 June 2025, a statutory notice had been gazetted under the Land (Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance, requiring those affected to vacate by 12 September 2025. The department also said that even though the statutory deadline had long passed, the Government had, in line with the "people-oriented" principle, striven to provide a buffer period for relocation arrangements while not affecting the overall works schedule. The Lands Department went on to say that as certain parts of Cha Kwo Ling Village are located near slopes, in order to safeguard the safety of residents/users facing a higher risk of natural hazards, a joint operation was carried out on 12 August to require villagers to vacate the site.
